claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. Just the one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your child, Alex.

To help me assess your eligibility, I need to ask:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

Now I need to understand your living situation:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that.

I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment. Let me start with:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and maintenance?** (This means you provide the main financial support for Alex's upbringing.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex's care and maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's important to know.

Now I need to check your residency status:

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

I just need to clarify one more important detail:

**Are you currently receiving any other benefits, such as Universal Credit, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or income support?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any other benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Before I give you my final assessment, let me just verify one more detail to ensure I have the complete picture:

**Is there anyone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, could Alex's other parent or another family member be claiming for the same child?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review the rules and provide you with my outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the information you've provided and the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

✓ **Alex is under 16** – At 8 years old, Alex meets the age requirement  
✓ **Alex lives with you** – You have confirmed Alex lives in your household  
✓ **You are responsible for their care and maintenance** – You provide the financial support for Alex  
✓ **You are a British citizen living in the UK** – You meet the residency requirements  
✓ **No one else is claiming for Alex** – Only one person can claim per child, and you have confirmed no one else is claiming  

You should now be able to apply for Child Benefit. If you haven't already, you can make a claim through the official government service. If you have any questions about the application process or your specific circumstances change, you can contact HMRC for further support.
